rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj transmits an unnamed explanation: God told angels humanity would corrupt and shed blood; they asked why, expecting creatures to glorify and purify God like them, and the disclosure confirmed divine knowledge of the unseen.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج حكاية عن غيره: المعنى في هذا هو (¬1): أن الله أعلم الملائكة أنه جاعل في الأرض خليفة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The missing divine announcement is inferred from the angels' answer: the text omits it for concision, as al-Shanfara's poetry also omits an understood phrase.
rows.anchor: فإن قيل: فأين إخبار الله بذلك للملائكة فإنا لا نراه في القرآن؟ قيل: هو محذوف مكتفى بدلالة الكلام عليه

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: The angels may have asked to learn the wisdom, not objected: after the jinn were removed, they occupied earth and asked why corrupting humans would replace them.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج: ويجوز أن يكون هذا القول من الملائكة على وجه استعلام وجه الحكمة، لا على الإنكار.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and most commentators say angels compared Adam's descendants with corrupting jinn; God knew Iblis's pride and delusion, and angels later admitted ignorance when unable to name things.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس وأكثر المفسرين: إن الله تعالى لما اطلع على كبر إبليس قال للملائكة الذين كانوا معه:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent address suggests the creation troubled angels: their worship had lightened while they lived on earth, and they feared returning to heaven, where worship would burden them again.
rows.anchor: ومع وضوح هذه الأقوال فإن ظاهر الخطاب يدل على أنه شق على الملائكة خلق الخليفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tasbih means declaring God free of every evil, and it can also mean prayer; to glorify God is to pray to Him.
rows.anchor: معنى التسبيح: تنزيه الله من كل سوء، وقد يكون بمعنى الصلاة، ويقال: سبح لله

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan explains the angels' phrase as saying, Subhan Allah wa bihamdihi.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن: معناه: يقول سبحان الله وبحمده

rows.speaker: الأزهري
rows.claim: Al-Azhari says exegetes and linguists agree that tasbih means declaring God transcendent and free of evil.
rows.anchor: قال الأزهري (¬4): أجمع المفسرون وأهل المعاني: أن معنى (¬5) تسبيح الله، تنزيه الله وتبرئته عن السوء.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word's root means distancing; anyone praising God and distancing Him from evil has glorified and purified Him.
rows.anchor: وأصل التسبيح (¬6) في اللغة، التبعيد من قولك: سبحت في الأرض، إذا تباعدت فيها

rows.speaker: بعض أهل المعاني
rows.claim: Some linguists explain tasbih with praise as speaking God's praise: praise and gratitude themselves honor Him and acknowledge His worthiness to be purified and exalted.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض أهل المعاني: معنى قوله: {نسبح بحمدك} نتكلم بالحمد لك، والنطق بالحمد لله تسبيح له،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Subhan Allah means God's freedom from evil and became an exclamation of wonder; al-A'sha's verse uses it to express astonishment.
rows.anchor: ومعنى قول القائل (سبحان الله): براءة الله من السوء (¬3) وتنزيهه، وكثر لفظ (سبحان الله) في كلامهم،

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj gives the concise sense of the angels' words as declaring God free of evil.
rows.anchor: ونحو هذا قال الزجاج في معنى: {نسبح بحمدك} قال: نبرئك من السوء

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، الحسن، قتادة
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, al-Hasan, and Qatada say angels had boasted that no creation would surpass them, so God favored Adam over them by teaching him the names.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس والحسن وقتادة: لما قال الله عز وجل للملائكة: {إني جاعل في الأرض خليفة} قالوا فيما بينهم:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God taught Adam by originating knowledge of the names in his heart and inspiring him with it.
rows.anchor: أن خلق في قلبه علما بالأسماء على سبيل الابتداء،

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas derives Adam's name from the face of the earth from which he was created.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: إنما سمي آدم، لأنه خلق من أديم الأرض

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj reports the linguists' derivation of Adam from the earth's surface because Adam was created from soil; adim is its face.
rows.anchor: الزجاج عنهم، قال: يقول أهل اللغة في آدم: إن اشتقاقه من أديم الأرض، لأنه خلق من تراب،

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra says adama in people denotes a dusky complexion, while in camels and gazelles it denotes whiteness; he had not heard a male gazelle called Adam.
rows.anchor: أبو عبيد عن الفراء قال: الأدمة في الناس شربة من سواد، وفي الإبل والظباء بياض،

rows.speaker: ذو الرمة
rows.claim: Dhu al-Rumma's verse uses adma for a gazelle, illustrating the feminine form of the color term.
rows.anchor: وقال ذو الرمة: من المؤلفات الرمل أدماء حرة

rows.speaker: الأعشى
rows.claim: Al-A'sha's verse applies adma to a she-camel.
rows.anchor:
وقال الأعشى في الناقة:
فقلت له هذه هاتها

rows.speaker: النضر بن شميل
rows.claim: Al-Nadr ibn Shumayl instead says Adam was named for being white in complexion.
rows.anchor: وقال النضر بن شميل: سمي آدم، لأنه كان أبيض اللون

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، مجاهد، قتادة، الضحاك
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Qatada, and al-Dahhak say Adam learned the name of every thing, down to a bowl and spoon.
rows.anchor: فقال ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة والضحاك: علمه اسم كل شيء حتى القصعة والمغرفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unrestricted wording indicates that Adam learned all names and every language, since anything named in any language falls under all names.
rows.anchor: وظاهر اللفظ يدل على هذا، وعلى أنه علمه جميع اللغات، لأنه قال: الأسماء كلها،

rows.speaker: جماعة من أهل التأويل
rows.claim: Some exegetes say Adam learned every language; his children later took distinct languages as they dispersed, so all languages were learned from him.
rows.anchor: على أنه قد قال جماعة من أهل التأويل: إن الله تعالى علم آدم

rows.speaker: الزجاجي
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaji divides names into ten kinds: concrete things, verbal nouns, labels, times, places, agents, patients, qualities, pronouns and demonstratives, and Arabic verbal nouns such as صه and هيهات.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاجي في قوله: {وعلم آدم الأسماء كلها}: الأسماء (¬3) على كثرتها عشرة أقسام (¬4)، فمنها: أسماء الأشخاص

rows.speaker: الزجاجي
rows.claim: Names generally were intended to fit their referents through meanings; labels such as Zayd and Amr identify individuals without describing them, even if Zayd derives from increase.
rows.anchor: فإن قولنا: (زيد) وإن كان مأخوذا من الزيادة فليس بحاو على مسماه لهذا المعنى،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Frequently used names yield known meanings, origins, figurative senses and derivatives; less-used names become opaque, although they too originally had a sound meaning.
rows.anchor: ولما صدقت العناية ببعض الأسماء دون بعض، أدرك معاني بعضها وموضوعه وحقيقته ومجازه وأصله وفرعه،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root meaning of عرض is to show or make something manifest; it is used of displaying goods, troops and a book.
rows.anchor: ومعنى العرض في اللغة: الإظهار، ومنه عرض الجارية وعرض الجند

rows.speaker: الليث
rows.claim: Al-Layth says a'rada means that something appeared; the cited poem uses a'radat for something becoming visible.
rows.anchor: الليث: ويقال: أعرض الشيء أي: بدا وظهر، وأنشد:

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra interprets God's display of Hell as making it visible; the intransitive form a'radat means it appeared, while عرضت الشيء is transitive and caused it to appear.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء في قوله تعالى: {وعرضنا جهنم يومئذ للكافرين عرضا (100)} [الكهف: 100]، أي أبرزناها حتى رأوها.

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil says God created all beings, animate and inanimate, taught Adam their names, then showed the actual entities to the angels; the pronoun refers to named things, including rational beings.
rows.anchor: فالجواب ما قال مقاتل: وهو أن الله تعالى خلق كل شيء، الحيوان والجماد ثم علم آدم أسماءها،

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says the names taught to Adam were the names of his descendants, so the display was of the descendants.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: علمه أسماء ذريته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anbiuni is a challenge meant to expose incapacity: the angels guessed about what they were not taught, while Adam received knowledge, so God asks how they claim knowledge of the unseen future when they do not know what they see.
rows.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {فقال أنبئوني}. أمر تعجيز (¬1)، كقوله: {فأتوا بسورة من مثله}

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، ناس من الصحابة
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and some Companions take if you are truthful to mean: if your claim that the future earthly deputy will corrupt and shed blood is true.
rows.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {إن كنتم صادقين}. أي: إن صدقتم أن الخليفة الذي أجعله في الأرض يفسد فيها ويسفك الدماء قاله ابن عباس،

rows.speaker: الحسن، قتادة
rows.claim: Al-Hasan and Qatada understand the challenge as testing whether the angels were right that no creation would be more knowledgeable or excellent than them.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: إن كنتم صادقين أني لا أخلق خلقا إلا كنتم أعلم وأفضل منه، وكذلك قال قتادة

rows.speaker: أبو عبيد، الكسائي، أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu Ubayd, citing al-Kisa'i and Abu Ubayda, says wafaytu and awfaytu both mean that one fulfilled a covenant.
rows.anchor: أبو عبيد عن الكسائي وأبي عبيدة: وفيت بالعهد وأوفيت به سواء

rows.speaker: شمر
rows.claim: Shammar distinguishes wafaa as a statement or measure reaching completion, while awfaa means fully paying another's right or measure without shortfall.
rows.anchor: يقال: وفى وأوفى، فمن قال: (وفى) فإنه يقول تم، كقولك: وفى لنا فلان، أي: تم لنا قوله ولم يغدر،

rows.speaker: أبو الهيثم
rows.claim: Abu al-Haytham rejects Shammar's distinction: both forms mean fulfilling a covenant, and Quranic examples use the form with alif.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو الهيثم فيما رد على شمر: الذي قال شمر (¬5) في (وفى) و (أوفى): باطل، إنما يقال: أوفيت بالعهد ووفيت بالعهد،

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: The cited line combines awfa and wafa, illustrating both forms in use.
rows.anchor: وقال الشاعر (¬4) في الجمع بين اللغتين:

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the covenant as the Torah's promise of Muhammad: believers receive two rewards for following Moses and Muhammad, while rejecters face accumulated sins and Hell; God promises Paradise for fulfilling it regarding Muhammad.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: هذا العهد هو أن الله عز وجل (¬6) عهد إليهم في التوراة أنه باعث نبيا يقال له: محمد،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iyyaya is accusative under an implicit verb, explained by the following farhabun; the explicit verb cannot govern it because that verb is occupied by its object pronoun.
rows.anchor: موضع (إياي) نصب بإضمار فعل (¬1) تفسيره (¬2) المذكور بعده (¬3) كأنه قيل: (إياي فارهبوا (¬4) فارهبون)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final ya is omitted from farhabun to preserve the verse ending's cadence; language scholars call verse endings fawasil and poetic line endings qawafi.
rows.anchor: وحذفت (الياء) من {فارهبون} لأنها فاصلة أي رأس آية، ليكون النظم على لفظ متسق،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command means to fear God by breaking the covenant.
rows.anchor: ومعناه: فخافوني في نقض العهد

rows.speaker: أبو عبيد
rows.claim: Abu Ubayd derives sabr from restraint, explaining expressions for holding a killer, a person held for execution, self-restraint and an oath imposed by keeping someone there; Antara's verse illustrates restraint.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبيد (¬1): أصل الصبر الحبس، وكل من حبس شيئا فقد صبره،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seek help through patience in performing obligations, avoiding forbidden acts, bearing harm and calamities, and fighting enemies; prayer helps because it restrains indecency and wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: ومعنى الآية: استعينوا بالصبر على أداء الفرائض واجتناب المحارم واحتمال الأذى وجهاد العدو وعلى المصائب والصلاة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid interprets patience here as fasting; Ramadan is called the month of patience and the fasting person a patient one.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: الصبر في هذه الآية الصوم، ويقال لشهر رمضان شهر الصبر، وللصائم صابر

rows.speaker: الحسن، الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Hasan and al-Dahhak explain kabira as heavy or burdensome.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن والضحاك: ثقيلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The underlying analogy is that what is big is heavy to carry, so anything psychologically difficult can be called big, as in the verse about what is urged on polytheists.
rows.anchor: والأصل في ذلك أن ما يكبر

rows.speaker: المؤرج
rows.claim: Al-Muarrij says the singular pronoun refers to prayer, the dominant, best and most important of the two; examples show a predicate agreeing with one of two named items.
rows.anchor: وقال: {وإذا رأوا تجارة أو لهوا انفضوا إليها} [الجمعة: 11]، هذا قول المؤرج (¬2).

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash says the pronoun applies distributively to each of patience and prayer, as the verse calls Mary and her son a sign while meaning each individually.
rows.anchor: وقال الأخفش (¬3): الكناية راجعة إلى كل واحد منهما، أراد وإن كل خصلة منها لكبيرة،

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: An unnamed poet's line is cited as evidence for a singular predicate applying to both coordinated terms distributively.
rows.anchor: كقوله: {وجعلنا ابن مريم وأمه آية} [المؤمنون: 50]، أراد كل واحد منهما قال الشاعر

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One explanation returns the pronoun to prayer because patience is included within prayer, as the Prophet's pleasure is included in God's pleasure.
rows.anchor: وقيل: رد الهاء إلى الصلاة، لأن الصبر داخل في الصلاة، كقوله: {والله ورسوله أحق أن يرضوه}

rows.speaker: الحسين بن الفضل
rows.claim: Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl says the pronoun refers to seeking help, since the command استعينوا implies that verbal noun.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسين بن الفضل: رد الكناية إلى الاستعانة، لأن (استعينوا) يدل على المصدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic can name two things and predicate only one, relying on that predicate to imply the other; the author illustrates this with Quranic examples and a poem contrasting viewpoints.
rows.anchor: والأصل في هذا وأمثاله أن العرب تذكر شيئين، ثم تخبر عن أيهما شاءت، فتكتفي بالخبر عن أحدهما عن الثاني،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khushu' originally means stillness; the verse says voices become still before the Merciful.
rows.anchor: أصل الخشوع في اللغة: السكون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A wall described as khashi' has collapsed and become level with the ground; al-Nabigha's verse illustrates the usage.
rows.anchor: ويقال: جدار خاشع، إذا تداعى واستوى مع الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report describes the Kaaba as still upon the water, illustrating the same basic sense of khushu'.
rows.anchor: ومنه الحديث (كانت الكعبة خشعة على الماء)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word extends to land that stays dry and does not sprout, a meaning illustrated by the verse about barren-looking earth receiving rain.
rows.anchor: فقيل: خشعت الأرض، إذا لم تمطر، فلم تهتز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other extensions describe a hump losing fat and drooping, eyes lowered without glancing, and a submissive worshipper whose stillness reflects obedience.
rows.anchor: وخشع السنام، إذا ذهب شحمه وتطأطأ شرفه. وخشعت الأبصار، إذا سكنت ونظرت في الأرض من غير التفات.

rows.speaker: أصحاب المعاني
rows.claim: All forms of worship are covered by patience, meaning steadfastness in them; prayer is singled out to emphasize its distinction, as fruit, palm and pomegranate and angels, messengers, Gabriel and Michael are singled out.
rows.anchor: قال المفسرون وأصحاب المعاني: إن (¬6) جميع العبادات داخلة تحت قوله:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If patience means fasting, fasting and prayer answer barriers to Islam: greed and fear of losing food or leadership; fasting curbs greed, while prayer brings humility and removes arrogance and status-seeking.
rows.anchor: وعلى قول من يقول: الصبر هو الصوم (¬1)، فإنما خص الصوم والصلاة، لأن القوم إنما كان يمنعهم عن الإسلام الشره وخوف ذهاب مأكلتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The intended prayer is prayer joined with belief in Muhammad, which was difficult for unbelievers.
rows.anchor: وأريد بالصلاة الصلاة التي معها الإيمان بحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم لأنها كانت

rows.speaker: أكثر أهل العلم
rows.claim: Most scholars say the address is to the People of the Book, while its instruction remains proper for all worshippers.
rows.anchor: وعند أكثر أهل العلم أن الآية خطاب لأهل الكتاب (¬8)، وهو مع ذلك أدب لجميع العباد

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say the address is to Muslims, who are told to seek God's pleasure, reward and Paradise through patient observance of obligations; the author says the People of the Book reading is clearer.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم: يرجع هذا القول إلى خطاب المسلمين فأمروا أن يستعينوا

rows.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
rows.claim: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib says the people had grown tired of their way of life.
rows.anchor: قال # سعيد بن المسيب: ملوا عيشهم

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says they remembered their former Egyptian food and asked Moses to pray for it; ta'am is a generic term for what is eaten.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: ذكر القوم عيشا كان لهم بمصر، فقالوا لموسى:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They called it one food because manna with quail was eaten together like one dish and presented as one color, although made from different ingredients.
rows.anchor: وإنما قالوا: طعام واحد، وكان طعامهم المن والسلوى، لأنهم كانوا يأكلون المن

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says manna was their food and quail their drink, but the two were combined when eaten and therefore counted as one food.
rows.anchor: قال ابن زيد: كان (¬5) طعامهم المن، وشرابهم السلوى،

rows.speaker: أصحاب المعاني
rows.claim: Some linguists say food was called one because their daily nourishment never changed, like someone described as following one regular course by keeping to fasting and prayer.
rows.anchor: وقال أصحاب المعاني: لما كان غذاؤهم في كل يوم لا يتغير، قيل: طعام واحد،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dua means asking one who can grant benefit or harm; it is named for the call used by a petitioner.
rows.anchor: معنى الدعاء: الطلب (¬1) ممن يملك النفع والضر.

rows.speaker: ابن السراج
rows.claim: Ibn al-Sarraj says dua originally means calling; a request is called dua because the petitioner says Lord and calls upon God.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن السراج: أصله النداء وإنما قال للمسألة: دعاء؛ لأن السائل يقول: يا رب، فينادي ربه عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The petition is expressed in the past tense as an optimistic expression that it has already happened.
rows.anchor: وجاء الدعاء بلفظ الماضي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yukhrij means asking God to bring something out; the following imperfect serves as the response to the preceding command, as in two cited verses.
rows.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {يخرج لنا} المعنى سله وقل له: أخرج (¬6) يخرج، وكذلك قوله: {وقل لعبادي يقولوا التي هي أحسن}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baql is any plant that does not retain a stalk after livestock graze it.
rows.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {من بقلها} البقل: كل نبات لا يبقى له ساق

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra says fawm is an old word for wheat and bread; some Arabs also say fummu lana to mean bake bread for us, as in a verse by Ahihah ibn al-Jallah about sowing fawm.
rows.anchor: فقال الفراء: الفوم فيما يذكرون لغة قديمة، وهي الحنطة والخبز جميعا قد ذكرا، قال: وقال بعضهم: سمحت العرب من أهل اللغة يقولون:

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra prefers reading fawm as thum, garlic: Abdullah's reading with thā fits the neighboring lentils and onions, supported by dialectal interchange of fā' and thā.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء: وهي في قراءة عبد الله: (وثومها) بالثاء، وكأنه أشبه المعنيين بالصواب؛

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisa'i also chooses the interpretation of fawm as garlic.
rows.anchor: وهذا القول أيضا اختيار الكسائي

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says fawm means wheat, or grain generally, and rejects garlic as unknown and implausible because the people sought staple food containing grain.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج: الفوم: الحنطة، ويقال: الحبوب، لا اختلاف بين أهل اللغة أن الفوم: الحنطة.

rows.speaker: اللحياني
rows.claim: Al-Lihyani says fum and thum both refer to wheat.
rows.anchor: وقال اللحياني: هو الفوم والثوم (¬5)، للحنطة

rows.speaker: ابن دريد، المبرد
rows.claim: Ibn Durayd says the Azd of al-Sarat call the wheat ear fawm; al-Mubarrad chooses this explanation.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن دريد: أزد السراة يسمون السنبل فوما (¬8). وهذا القول اختيار # المبرد.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object of yukhrij is omitted and understood as something from the earth's plants; the same kind of omitted object occurs in the verse about Abraham's descendants.
rows.anchor: ومفعول (يخرج) محذوف من الكلام، تقديره: يخرج لنا مما تنبت الأرض من بقلها شيئا

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj prefers adna from nearness: the people would exchange a readily available, ordinary food for the noble provision specially granted them over others.
rows.anchor: والأول (¬5) اختيار الزجاج (¬6).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading takes adna as nearer in value, meaning of lesser worth, or as less tasty and pleasurable than what was better.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون معنى الدنو في قرب القيمة (¬5)، يقول: أتستبدلون الذي هو أقرب في القيمة (¬6)،

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra also derives adna from baseness, with Zuhayr al-Farqabi reportedly reading it adna'a with hamza.
rows.anchor: على أنه قد حكى الفراء (¬1) عن زهير الفرقبي (¬2) أنه يقرأ (أدنأ) بالهمز

rows.speaker: بعض النحويين
rows.claim: Some grammarians explain adna as adwan, meaning lower or meaner, by swapping n and w; the author rejects this because dun meaning inferior does not yield a verb.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض النحويين: (أدنى) هاهنا بمعنى أدون، أي: أوضع وأخس، فقدمت النون وحولت الواو ألفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to descend to Misr may be spoken by Moses, or by God after an omitted prayer and response.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى: {اهبطوا مصرا} جائز أن يكون هذا من كلام موسى لهم (¬2)، وجائز أن يكون من قول الله تعالى لهم،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With tanwin, Misran can mean any city, since the requested produce was available in towns and cities.
rows.anchor: فإن الذي سألتم لا يكون إلا في القرى والأمصار، ولهذا نون مصر،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Misr may instead mean Egypt specifically; it could then take declension because the name is light and short.
rows.anchor: وجائز أن يكون أراد مصر بعينها، وصرفها لخفتها وقلة حروفها

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the name is declined because it is masculine and was given to a masculine place-name, like other short names.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج: صرف؛ لأنه مذكر سمي به مذكر (¬6)، فهو مثل جمل

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra prefers leaving Misr undeclined; unlike common feminine names of three letters with a still middle letter, a place-name is rarely used as a personal name, and its written alif marks pause.
rows.anchor: والفراء يختار ترك الإجراء، ويفرق بين هذا وبين أسماء النساء،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The noninflected reading is described as rare; the author favors inflection because the name is light and short.
rows.anchor: ويختار قراءة من قرأ مصر بغير تنوين (¬8)، وهي قرآءة مهجورة (¬9)، # والوجه ما ذكرنا قبل، أنه صرف لخفته

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisa'i says eloquent Arabs freely decline words normally treated as indeclinable, including in poetry; only comparatives on af'al are never heard declined.
rows.anchor: وقال الكسائي: العرب الفصحاء (¬2) لا يبالون أن يجروا مالا يجري،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Misr means a boundary; Adi ibn Zayd's verse makes the sun a boundary between day and night, and the word also means a house's limits or cultivated land separated from wilderness.
rows.anchor: والمصر في اللغة: الحاجز بين الشيئين (¬4).
